sources.name: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet
sources.used_for: gravity, temperature, distance in million km, Moon's distance from Earth

sources.name: NASA Mission Viz: orbital parameters table
sources.used_for: sma_au (distance from the Sun in AU) and period_days (length of a year), used for food and real trip times

rules.fuel: gravity (m/s^2) x 10  -> stronger gravity = more fuel
rules.food: sma_au (distance from Sun in AU, Mission Viz) x 10  -> farther = more food
rules.trip_days: Hohmann transfer from Earth: 0.5 x ((1 + sma_au) / 2)^1.5 x Earth's period_days. The Moon isn't in the Mission Viz table, so its trip uses the 3 days Apollo crews took. Europa orbits Jupiter, so it uses Jupiter's row.
rules.minutes: time on the surface to collect information (team idea: 3, 2, 1)
rules.from_earth: closest distance from Earth in million km (Moon: 0.384 from the fact sheet; planets: their distance from the Sun minus Earth's 149.6)

levels.note: Europa is a moon of Jupiter. It isn't in the Mission Viz table, so its distance, year and trip time use Jupiter's row. Gravity and temperature: check on NASA's Europa page (Diana).
